chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') who had intercourse with his wife and did not perform the Tawaf al-Ifadah (Ziyarah), and he said: 'He should slaughter a camel, and I fear that his Hajj may be deficient if he was knowledgeable, and if he was ignorant, there is no blame upon him.'

key_terms.ثُلِمَ حَجُّهُ: His Hajj was deficient or lacked completeness.
key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: There is no blame or harm.
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in the same season.
key_terms.يَزُرْ: To perform the Ziyarah (Tawaf al-Ifadah), the final circumambulation required to complete Hajj.
key_terms.يَنْحَرُ جَزُوراً: He slaughters a camel (as a fidya/penalty).

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a Mutamatti' pilgrim who has intercourse before performing Tawaf al-Ifadah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the penalty for a Mutamatti' who engages in marital relations before completing the Tawaf al-Ifadah, prescribing the slaughter of a camel (jazur). The Imam’s expression of concern ('khishya') regarding the Hajj being 'thulima' (deficient) highlights the Shia juristic distinction between major invalidation and minor deficiency based on the pilgrim's knowledge ('ilm') versus ignorance ('jahil'). This ruling underscores the importance of intention and awareness in the validity of Hajj rituals within the Ja'fari school of jurisprudence.
